title: Abraham, Moses and One God
welcome_lead: Trace Judaism's roots back to two of history's greatest figures: Abraham and Moses.
meta_desc: KS3 Religious Studies adventure on Abraham, Moses and the origins of Judaism.
final_note: You can now explain Abraham and Moses's roles in Jewish history.

concepts.def: Oldest Abrahamic faith; followers are Jews.
Founding patriarch of Judaism; trusted God.
Prophet who led Jews out of Egypt and received Torah.
Special agreement between God and the Jewish people.
Belief in only one God; central to Judaism.
Land promised by God; modern country since 1948.

walkthroughs.body_html: Judaism traces its beginning to Abraham, who according to the Torah trusted in one God. God made a covenant (special agreement) with Abraham, promising him many descendants and the land of Israel. Christianity and Islam also honour Abraham.

Centuries later, the Jewish people were enslaved in Egypt. God called Moses to lead them out — the Exodus — to freedom. At Mount Sinai, Moses received the Torah, including the Ten Commandments. This shaped Jewish law and life.

The most important Jewish prayer, the Shema, says: 'Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.' Judaism is strictly monotheistic and was the first major religion to teach belief in a single God.
